title: Money & happiness
subtitle: 金钱与幸福感
source: 2014 考研英语二 · 阅读理解 Text 1
sourceNote: 取自你提供的试题册，原书页码 2014-4 至 2014-5。外刊书评的考试改编材料。学习提示与例句为本原型编写。

sentences.zh: 如果你有 5.9 亿美元，你会拿它做什么？
parts: would
在假设情境中问“你会……？”；这里不是在说过去发生的事。
with $590m
with 表示对这笔钱的使用或处置。m 是 million（百万）的缩写：590 × 一百万 = 5.9 亿。

with: prep.
表示处理或使用的对象（do with money）
What will you do with this money?
你会怎么使用这笔钱？
do: 处理；使用（do with money：怎么使用钱）
What will you do with this money?

sentences.text: This is now a question for Gloria MacKenzie, an 84-year-old widow who recently emerged from her small, tin-roofed house in Florida to collect the biggest undivided lottery jackpot in history.
sentences.zh: 对于格洛丽亚·麦肯齐来说，这如今是一个现实的问题。这位 84 岁的寡妇最近走出她在佛罗里达州那间小小的铁皮屋顶房子，去领取有史以来由一人独得的最大奖额的彩票头奖。
sentences.main: This is now a question for Gloria MacKenzie.
parts: an 84-year-old widow
同位语：补充说明 Gloria 是谁。
who recently emerged …
定语从句，修饰 widow；who 是从句的主语。
to collect …
不定式表示目的：走出来是为了领奖。undivided 强调奖金没有分给多个中奖者。

for: prep.
对……而言
This is a serious question for her.
这对她来说是个重要问题。
in: 在……里；本句分别表示所在地和历史范围
She lives in Florida and studies events in its history.
她住在佛罗里达州，并研究该州历史上的事件。
to: infinitive marker
引出目的不定式：为了领取奖金
He went to collect his prize.
他去领取奖金。
undivided: 未分割的；本句指整笔奖金未由多人瓜分
He received the whole, undivided prize.
他获得了整笔未被瓜分的奖金。

sentences.text: If she hopes her new-found fortune will yield lasting feelings of fulfilment, she could do worse than read Happy Money by Elizabeth Dunn and Michael Norton.
sentences.zh: 如果她希望这笔新得的财富能带来持久的满足感，那么读一读伊丽莎白·邓恩和迈克尔·诺顿的《Happy Money》会是个不错的选择。
sentences.main: If she hopes …, she could do worse than read Happy Money.
parts: If she hopes …
条件从句；hopes 后省略了 that，后面的完整句子是她希望发生的事。
her new-found fortune will yield …
财富作主语；yield 作动词，意思是“带来”。
could do worse than …
委婉推荐：做某事不失为一个好选择，不应逐字翻成“比……做得更坏”。

worse: 更差；could do worse than 用来委婉地建议做某事
You could do worse than read this book.
读读这本书会是个不错的选择。
than: 与 worse 连用引出比较；could do worse than 是委婉建议
You could do worse than read this book.
读读这本书会是个不错的选择。

sentences.text: These two academics use an array of behavioural research to show that the most rewarding ways to spend money can be counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这两位学者利用一系列行为研究表明，最能带来满足感的花钱方式可能与直觉相反。
sentences.main: These two academics use research to show that …
parts: an array of
一系列；许多。
that the most rewarding ways …
show 的宾语从句：说明研究揭示了什么。
to spend money
修饰 ways，说明是“花钱的方式”；can be counterintuitive 是从句谓语。

rewarding: 带来满足感的；令人有收获的
that: 引导宾语从句，说明表明的内容
to: infinitive marker
两处引出不定式：to show 表目的；to spend 说明 ways
She used research to show better ways to spend money.
她利用研究说明更好的花钱方式。
most: 最；构成 rewarding 的最高级
This is the most rewarding task.
这是最能带来满足感的任务。

sentences.text: Fantasies of great wealth often involve visions of fancy cars and extravagant homes.
sentences.zh: 人们对巨额财富的幻想中，常常有豪车和奢华住宅的画面。
parts: of great wealth
修饰 Fantasies：关于巨额财富的幻想。
of fancy cars and extravagant homes
修饰 visions，说明脑海中浮现的是什么。

sentences.text: Yet satisfaction with these material purchases wears off fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 然而，购买这些物质商品带来的满足感消退得相当快。
parts: Yet
句首表示转折：“然而”。
with these material purchases
修饰 satisfaction，指对这些物质购买的满足感。
wears off
逐渐消退。这里不是衣服“穿旧了”。fairly quickly 表示“相当快地”。

with: prep.
表示满意所针对的对象（satisfaction with）
She felt satisfaction with her work.
她对自己的工作感到满意。
wears: 消退（与 off 构成 wears off）
off: 与 wear 连用表示逐渐消退（wear off）

sentences.text: What was once exciting and new becomes old-hat; regret creeps in.
sentences.zh: 曾经让人兴奋、觉得新鲜的东西变得稀松平常，后悔也悄悄出现。
sentences.main: What was once exciting and new becomes old-hat; regret creeps in.
parts: What was once exciting and new
整个 what 从句作主语：“曾经令人兴奋而新鲜的事物”。
becomes old-hat
变得老套、不再新鲜；old-hat 在这里作表语。
regret creeps in
分号连接另一个完整分句；后悔不知不觉出现。

what: 引导主语从句，表示“……的事物”
What once felt exciting now seems ordinary.
曾经令人兴奋的事物如今显得平常。
in: 与 creep 连用，表示悄然出现（creep in）
creeps: 悄然出现；逐渐产生（creep in）

sentences.text: It is far better to spend money on experiences, say Ms. Dunn and Mr. Norton, like interesting trips, unique meals or even going to the cinema.
sentences.zh: 邓恩女士和诺顿先生说，把钱花在体验上要好得多，比如有趣的旅行、别具一格的餐饮体验，甚至是去看电影。
sentences.main: It is far better to spend money on experiences.
parts: It is … to spend …
It 是形式主语，真正评价的事情是后面的“把钱花在体验上”。
say Ms. Dunn and Mr. Norton
插入的引述语，交代这个观点是谁说的。
like interesting trips …
like 表示“例如”，列举体验。far 修饰比较级 better，表示“好得多”。

It: 形式主语，指后面的 to spend …
better: 更好的；本句表示把钱花在体验上更好
It is better to spend less.
to: infinitive marker / prep.
两处用法：to spend 引出不定式；to the cinema 表去往的地点
It is better to go to the cinema.
去看电影会更好。
ms: 女士；用于女性姓氏前，不说明婚姻状况

sentences.text: These purchases often become more valuable with time—as stories or memories—particularly if they involve feeling more connected to others.
sentences.zh: 这些购买往往会随着时间变得更有价值，化为故事或回忆；尤其是当它们让人觉得与他人联系更紧密时。
sentences.main: These purchases often become more valuable with time.
parts: as stories or memories
破折号中补充说明它们以什么形式变得有价值。
particularly if …
尤其是在……的情况下，进一步限定。
involve feeling more connected to others
involve 后接动名词 feeling；connected 表示与他人有情感联系。

with: prep.
随着（时间推移）
Memories become more valuable with time.
回忆会随着时间变得更珍贵。
purchases: 购买；本句指购买体验的消费
A purchase of concert tickets can create lasting memories.
买演唱会门票能留下长久的回忆。
more: 更；分别修饰 valuable 和 connected，表示程度增加
Shared experiences can feel more valuable and make people more connected.
共同体验可以更有价值，也让人们联系更紧密。
they: 它们；指前文购买体验的消费
它们能留下长久的回忆。
to: prep.
表示联系的对象（connected to others）
Music helps us feel connected to others.
音乐帮助我们感受到与他人的联系。
connected: 音乐让我们感到彼此相连。

sentences.text: This slim volume is packed with tips to help wage slaves as well as lottery winners get the most “happiness bang for your buck”.
sentences.zh: 这本薄薄的书里满是实用建议，帮助上班族和彩票中奖者一样，让花出去的钱带来尽可能多的幸福。
sentences.main: This slim volume is packed with tips.
parts: to help … get …
说明建议的用途；help 后面的动词 get 可以不带 to。
wage slaves as well as lottery winners
两个并列的帮助对象。wage slaves 是带调侃意味的“为工资奔忙的人”。
happiness bang for your buck
借用“花的钱很值”的习语，强调每一分钱换来的幸福。

most: 最多的；修饰幸福回报，表示尽可能大的回报
These tips help you get the most enjoyment for your money.
这些建议能帮你用花出去的钱获得尽可能多的乐趣。
well: as well as 的组成词；整个表达表示“以及；和”
The guide helps students as well as teachers.
这份指南既帮助学生，也帮助教师。
slaves: 受工作和工资束缚的人（见 wage slaves）
with: prep.
与 packed 连用表示充满……
The book is packed with practical tips.
这本书满是实用建议。
to: infinitive marker
引出说明建议用途的不定式：用来帮助……
The guide offers tips to help beginners.
指南提供了帮助初学者的建议。
as: as well as 的组成词，表示“以及；和”
The guide helps students as well as teachers.
这份指南既帮助学生，也帮助教师。
bang: 回报；效果（bang for your buck：花钱获得的回报）
This course gives you more bang for your buck.
这门课让你花的钱获得更多回报。
for: prep.
连接所得回报与付出的金钱（bang for your buck）
This course gives you value for your money.
这门课让你花的钱有所值。
help: This tip can help you learn.
这个建议能帮助你学习。
packed: The book is packed with ideas.

sentences.text: It seems most people would be better off if they could shorten their commutes to work, spend more time with friends and family and less of it watching television (something the average American spends a whopping two months a year doing, and is hardly jollier for it).
sentences.zh: 看来，如果大多数人能缩短上下班通勤时间，多与朋友和家人相处，少看电视，他们的生活会更好。普通美国人一年竟花两个月看电视，却几乎没有因此变得更快乐。
sentences.main: It seems most people would be better off if …
parts: It seems (that) …
看来……；that 被省略。
if they could shorten …, spend …
条件从句列出缩短通勤、增加相处时间、减少看电视三个方面；less of it 中 it 指 time。
something the average American spends … doing
括号补充评论看电视；something 后省略了关系代词。
hardly jollier for it
几乎没有因此更快乐。hardly 是“几乎不”，不是“努力地”。

it: 本句三处：句首 It seems 的 It 是形式主语，引出后面的判断；less of it 的 it 回指 time（时间）；for it 的 it 回指 watching television（看电视这件事）。
It seems that exercise takes time, but spending some of it on walking can be good for you; you may feel better for it.
锻炼似乎需要时间，但拿出一点时间走走对你有好处；你可能因此感觉更好。
for: prep.
由于；表示看电视未让人更快乐的原因
She feels better for taking a walk.
散步后她感觉好多了。
off: 与 better 连用表示处境更好（be better off）
We would be better off with a shorter commute.
通勤时间更短，我们的处境会更好。
better: 更好；better off 表示处境更好
We would be better off with a shorter commute.
通勤时间更短，我们的处境会更好。
American: 一位美国人回答了问题。
doing: 做；本句指看电视这一活动
Watching television is what he spends hours doing.
他花好几个小时做的事就是看电视。
to: prep.
到；表示通勤的目的地（to work）
She walks to work.
她步行去上班。
less: 较少的部分；less of it 指较少的时间
She spent less of her time watching television.
她把较少的时间花在看电视上。
of: 表示整体中的一部分（less of it）
She spent less of her time watching television.
她把较少的时间花在看电视上。
a: 两处用法：a whopping two months 表示整整一段时间；a year 表示每年
It takes a full two hours a day.
每天要花足足两个小时。

sentences.text: Buying gifts or giving to charity is often more pleasurable than purchasing things for oneself, and luxuries are most enjoyable when they are consumed sparingly.
sentences.zh: 买礼物送人或向慈善机构捐赠，往往比为自己购物更令人愉快；而奢侈享受只有在适度、偶尔为之时，才最令人享受。
sentences.main: Buying … or giving … is more pleasurable …, and luxuries are most enjoyable …
parts: Buying gifts or giving to charity
动名词短语作第一个分句的主语。
than purchasing things for oneself
比较对象：“为自己购物”。
when they are consumed sparingly
时间／条件状语从句，they 指 luxuries；be consumed 是被动语态。

consumed: 享用；消费（本句用于被动语态）
We consume small amounts of chocolate.
for: prep.
为；给
purchasing: 购买（动名词，指购物活动）
购买奢侈品可能花费很高。
most: 最；修饰 enjoyable，表示最令人愉快
Small luxuries are most enjoyable when used sparingly.
小小的奢侈品在节制享用时最令人愉快。
to: prep.
表示捐赠的接受方（give to charity）
They give money to charity.
他们向慈善机构捐款。
more: 更；修饰 pleasurable，表示程度增加
Giving can be more pleasurable than buying for oneself.
赠予他人可能比给自己买东西更令人愉快。
they: They are enjoyable when used sparingly.
它们在节制享用时很令人愉快。
are: 与 consumed 构成被动语态：被享用
这些美食被节制地享用。
luxuries: 奢侈品；非必需的享受性物品
A designer bag is a luxury.

sentences.text: This is apparently the reason MacDonald’s restricts the availability of its popular McRib—a marketing trick that has turned the pork sandwich into an object of obsession.
sentences.zh: 这显然就是麦当劳限制其人气产品 McRib 供应的原因。这一营销手法，让这款猪肉三明治成了人们痴迷的对象。
parts: the reason MacDonald’s restricts …
reason 后省略了 why，后面说明是哪件事的原因。
a marketing trick
破折号后的补充说明，指限制供应这种手法。
that has turned … into …
定语从句修饰 trick；turn A into B 表示“把 A 变成 B”。

marketing: 营销；本句作定语修饰 trick
They tried a new marketing trick.
他们尝试了新的营销手法。
that: 引导定语从句，指前面的营销手法
This is a plan that saves time.
这是一个能节省时间的计划。
has: 与 turned 构成现在完成时
She has worked here for years.
into: 与 turn 连用表示转变的结果（turn into）

sentences.text: Readers of Happy Money are clearly a privileged lot, anxious about fulfilment, not hunger.
sentences.zh: 《Happy Money》的读者显然是一群生活优裕的人，他们担忧的是满足感，而不是饥饿。
sentences.main: Readers of Happy Money are clearly a privileged lot.
parts: a privileged lot
lot 在这里指“一群人”，privileged 指处境优越、有优势的。
anxious about fulfilment, not hunger
形容词短语补充说明这群人的状态，含有对其优裕处境的提醒。

happy: 快乐的（这里属于书名 Happy Money）
of: 连接读者与所读的书（readers of）
Readers of the book shared their views.
这本书的读者分享了看法。
about: She is anxious about the future.

sentences.text: Money may not quite buy happiness, but people in wealthier countries are generally happier than those in poor ones.
sentences.zh: 金钱未必真能买来幸福，但较富裕国家的人通常比贫穷国家的人更幸福。
sentences.main: Money may not quite buy happiness, but people … are generally happier …
parts: may not quite
语气有保留：未必完全能……。
people in wealthier countries
people 是主语，后面的介词短语说明是哪些人。
those in poor ones
those 代指 people，ones 代指 countries，避免重复。

those: 那些人；指贫穷国家的人们
Those in the front row can see clearly.
ones: Some countries are rich; other ones are poor.
有些国家富裕，另一些国家贫穷。
quite: 完全；真正（与 not 连用）
in: 在；两处均表示人们所在的国家
People in rich countries may differ from those in poor ones.
富裕国家的人可能与贫穷国家的人不同。

sentences.text: Yet the link between feeling good and spending money on others can be seen among rich and poor people around the world, and scarcity enhances the pleasure of most things for most people.
sentences.zh: 然而，给别人花钱与良好感受之间的联系，在世界各地的富人和穷人身上都能看到；对大多数人来说，稀缺性也会增强大多数事物带来的愉悦感。
sentences.main: The link … can be seen …, and scarcity enhances the pleasure …
parts: between feeling good and spending money on others
between A and B，说明哪两件事之间的联系。
can be seen among …
情态动词加被动语态：能在这些人身上被观察到。
scarcity enhances …
第二分句提出另一个观点：稀缺性增强愉悦感。

between: 连接相关的两方面：愉快感受与为他人花钱
There is a link between money and happiness.
金钱与幸福之间有关联。
be: 与 seen 构成被动语态（can be seen）
The pattern can be seen among different groups.
可以在不同群体中看到这种模式。
rich: Rich people can still worry about money.
富裕的人仍可能担忧金钱。
for: prep.
对……而言
This is enjoyable for most people.
这对大多数人来说很愉快。

sentences.text: Not everyone will agree with the authors’ policy ideas, which range from mandating more holiday time to reducing tax incentives for American homebuyers.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都会赞同作者的政策主张，其中既包括强制增加休假时间，也包括减少给美国购房者的税收优惠。
sentences.main: Not everyone will agree with the authors’ policy ideas.
parts: Not everyone
部分否定：“并非每个人”，不是“所有人都不”。
which range from … to …
非限制性定语从句，补充说明 policy ideas 的范围。
mandating … / reducing …
from 和 to 都是介词，后面接动名词。

with: prep.
表示赞同的对象（agree with）
I agree with the authors' ideas.
我赞同作者们的观点。
to: prep.
到；range from … to … 表示范围的终点
The options range from rest to exercise.
选择范围从休息到锻炼。
authors’: 作者们的（名词复数所有格）
作者们的观点引发了讨论。
tax: They pay tax on their income.
which: 引导非限制性定语从句，指这些政策主张
from: 从；range from … to … 表示范围的起点
The options range from rest to exercise.
选择范围从休息到锻炼。
mandating: 强制规定；要求必须提供（动名词）
Mandating paid leave is one option.
规定必须提供带薪休假是一种选择。
for: prep.
表示政策优惠所面向的对象
The tax incentives are for homebuyers.
这些税收优惠面向购房者。

sentences.text: But most people will come away from this book believing it was money well spent.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人读完这本书后，会觉得买书的钱花得很值。
sentences.main: Most people will come away … believing …
parts: come away from this book
这里指读完书后带着某种印象或收获，不是“远离这本书”。
believing it was money well spent
现在分词短语说明读者读后的想法；believing 后省略了 that。
money well spent
spent 是过去分词，后置修饰 money：花得值得的钱。

spent: 花费（金钱）；well spent 指花得值得
it: I paid for the course, and it was money well spent.
我花钱报了这门课，这笔钱花得很值。
well: 值得地；恰当地（修饰 spent）
come: 与 away from 连用：读罢后产生某种印象
Readers come away from the book feeling hopeful.
读者读完书后满怀希望。
away: come away from 的组成词；表示读罢后带着某种感受
Readers come away from the book feeling hopeful.
读者读完书后满怀希望。
from: 与 come away 连用，表示产生读后感的来源
